sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Jena's central policy is to make the street dearer so that drivers use garages. From 1 February 2025 the city raised on-street parking charges by 50% in all three zones, to €3.00 an hour in the centre, €1.50 in Zone 2 and €0.75 in Zone 3 [0][1]. At the same time the annual resident permit rose from €30.70 to €120 [2]. The city said the aim was to "motivate visitors" to use the multi-storey and underground car parks more, noting that an hour of street parking in the centre now costs more than a single bus or tram ticket at €2.70, and that private garages average about €1 to €2.50 an hour. It earmarked the revenue for climate measures [3].

Resident parking has been hard to extend. In February 2022 the council decided that new resident zones will only be ordered if the extra money and staff can be found, after the administration reported that extending them was costly and not refinanceable [4]. The existing zones date from 1992 to 2019, and building on the large surface car parks, among them Eichplatz, mainly reduces resident spaces in the centre [5]. Jena has no public park-and-ride system; the city points drivers to cheaper outer car parks with a maximum of €4.50 a day [16]. Electric cars with an E plate may park free in marked spaces at several central car parks [17]. Naumburger Straße was due to be rebuilt from March 2026, with a full closure until the end of November and the tram extended to Himmelreich [14].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
New capacity has been difficult to fund. A February 2022 council paper put a garage of about 450 spaces on the Seidelstraße car park at no less than €11 million, and a 2018 study found it could not be refinanced; the plan stalled after a citizens' initiative and for lack of a political majority and funding [7]. In July 2022 the council decided to reduce the planned Inselplatz parking facility, partly offsetting it with an extra underground level at Eichplatz and reserving land at Anger 26 and Seidelstraße, and asked the mayor to show options for about 200 spaces at Inselplatz [8]. The city later said a pure garage at Am Anger looked uneconomic at current construction prices [10]. The Inselplatz garage was meant to serve the university's new Campus Inselplatz, under construction since March 2020, with the remaining buildings due by the end of 2026 [10][11].

Demand is not obviously short of space. The same council papers describe the garage at the Wiesencenter as largely empty all day on several levels. They add that the planned changes create a calculated deficit in the eastern centre, though whether it becomes real "remains to be seen" [9]. Technology is coming slowly: the city's parking page shows live free-space counts for some garages and says the service is to be extended as part of a new guidance system [15]. Public charging has grown to over 120 public points, and the utility cut its public charging prices from January 2026 [18][19]. We found no sourced figures on a shift from the centre to shopping centres.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our Jena data cover ten car parks with 1,676 spaces, six of them within 500 m of the Markt with 1,348 spaces. Seven are within 500 m of Jena Paradies station. Our data lists the city as operator of three: Eichplatz (300 spaces, €3.00 an hour), Seidelparkplatz (161, €1.50, maximum €4.50 a day) and the small Haeckelplatz (32, €3.00). Eichplatz and Seidelparkplatz are surface car parks [1][5]. The private operators are few. APCOA runs the Goethe Galerie, the largest at 523 spaces on the city's page (APCOA lists 740), at €1.50 for each of the first two hours and €20 a day [22]. A third-party directory lists Contipark as operator of the Krautgasse garage (200 spaces on the city's page, 381 in the directory) [23]. Contipark also runs the 1,300-space garage at the university hospital, at €2.20 an hour, which is outside our measured set [20][21]. The operators of Holzmarkt, Neue Mitte and Windberg are not stated on the source pages.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 33% on weekdays and 27% at weekends. The fullest are Haeckelplatz (83% on weekdays, 32 spaces), City Carree (76%, 40 spaces) and Neue Mitte (70%, 165 spaces, €1.00 an hour, the cheapest). Price and occupancy do not line up. Haeckelplatz is among the dearest and the fullest, while the Goethe Galerie, the largest car park, is only 22% full on weekdays and 6% at weekends. Within 500 m of the Markt the average is 35% on weekdays, against 9% for the two car parks more than 2 km out.

The data cover the summer holidays and the university break, so term-time figures may differ. Capacities disagree between sources for several car parks, and history is patchy, so we make no year-on-year claim for Jena.
